Response time of a calibrated model

Source: R/response_time.R
pdm_response_time.Rd

Measures how quickly a model's catchment responds to rain, by experiment rather than by formula, so it works for any structure. The model starts in steady state at a reference flow, a single pulse of rain falls in the first time step, and the extra flow it causes is traced until it has nearly gone. A second run without the pulse is subtracted, so the recession the model was already in does not count.

Usage

pdm_response_time(
  model,
  flow,
  baseflow_fraction = 0.7,
  pulse_mm = 10,
  max_hours = 24 * 60,
  feh_time_to_peak_h = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A FlodePdmModel.

flow

Reference flow in m3/s at which the catchment starts, in steady state.

baseflow_fraction

Share of the reference flow that is baseflow, as in initial_state_from_flow().

pulse_mm

Depth of the rain pulse in mm, falling in the first time step.

max_hours

Longest response to trace, in hours.

feh_time_to_peak_h

Optional FEH time to peak in hours, for comparison.

Value

A list: time_to_peak_h, recession_h, centroid_lag_h, peak_m3s (extra flow at the peak), dt (model step, h), response (a data.frame of time in hours from the pulse centre and the extra flow) and, when FEH is given, feh (time to peak, ratio and flag).

Details

ResultMeaning
time_to_peak_hFrom the middle of the pulse to the peak of the extra flow
recession_hFrom the peak until the extra flow falls to 1/e (37 per cent) of it
centroid_lag_hFrom the middle of the pulse to the centre of mass of the extra flow

The time to peak is interpolated between steps with a parabola through the peak.

The answer depends on how wet the catchment is, because the soil store decides how much of the pulse runs off and the groundwater store may be nonlinear. Give the reference flow you care about: a typical flood flow for forecasting, the median for general use.

Comparing with FEH. If feh_time_to_peak_h is given, from catchment descriptors (for example reach.postproc::feh_time_to_peak()), the two are compared. A ratio outside 0.5 to 2 is flagged: either the model's fast stores or the descriptors deserve a look. The model's own figure is the better guide for that model, because it reflects the calibration; the FEH figure is an independent check.

See also

ar_from_response_time(), pdm_hindcast()

Examples

model <- pdm_model(area_km2 = 50)
rt <- pdm_response_time(model, flow = 5)
rt[c("time_to_peak_h", "recession_h", "centroid_lag_h")]
#> $time_to_peak_h
#> [1] 16.40128
#> 
#> $recession_h
#> [1] 41.34123
#> 
#> $centroid_lag_h
#> [1] 55.75434
#>
